characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe: MCU Peter Parker has never bonded with the symbiote on screen; the only MCU symbiote material is the fragment left behind in the Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021) mid-credits scene. Symbiote traits such as tendrils or sonic/heat weakness come from comics and non-MCU films, not MCU footage.
characters.summary: A form not depicted in the MCU. In No Way Home's mid-credits scene, Eddie Brock is sent home by Doctor Strange's spell and a piece of the symbiote breaks away and crawls off in the MCU world. MCU Peter Parker is never shown wearing it, so this form has no MCU-shown feats.

techniques: Not established on screen for this form

mechanisms: Not established on screen for this form

mobility: Not established on screen for this form
limitations: Form never depicted in the MCU; no on-screen capabilities to cite
characters.formDifferences: Would replace Peter Parker's Stark/integrated suits with the alien symbiote. In the MCU this bonding has not happened: only an unbonded symbiote fragment is shown, left behind in the No Way Home mid-credits scene.

sources.supports: No Way Home mid-credits scene: Eddie/Venom sent home, a symbiote fragment breaks off and crawls away; no statement that MCU Peter wears it.

unknowns: Original record described symbiote tendril strikes, symbiote regenerative durability, boosted strength/aggression, and weaknesses to sonic vibrations and extreme heat. These are comics / non-MCU film traits not shown for MCU Spider-Man; removed pending an on-screen MCU depiction.
Base Spider-Man abilities (web-slinging, Spider-Sense) could not be checked: the cited MCU wiki Spider-Man page could not be opened.
Whether this roster form should exist in the MCU pool at all, given the MCU has not shown Peter Parker bonding with the symbiote.

characters.summary: Sprite is an Eternal with superhuman strength, stamina and speed who casts lifelike illusions. In Eternals she projected an illusion of Ajak to distract Sersi before stabbing her with a dagger, and was later knocked out by Druig. Sersi ultimately transmuted her into a human.

techniques: Dagger attack (stabbed Sersi after an illusion distraction)

mechanisms: Eternal physiology (strength, stamina, speed beyond a normal human)

weaknesses: Can be overpowered physically (knocked out by Druig)
limitations: Illusions only; no reality alteration shown
Lost her Eternal powers after being transmuted into a human at the end of Eternals

sources.supports: Eternal physiology (strength, stamina, speed), longevity, and lifelike illusion casting.
Sprite's Ajak illusion and dagger attack on Sersi, Druig knocking her out, and Sersi transmuting her into a human.

feats.claim: Projected an illusion of Ajak to distract Sersi before stabbing her with a dagger.

notableResults.note: Druig recovered and knocked Sprite out during the confrontation over Tiamut's emergence.

unknowns: Original feat 'created massive illusions of cities and battles' is not supported by the opened pages; removed.
Flight/levitation, memory concealment and knife-combat skill were not supported by the opened pages; removed (flight tag dropped).
Outcome of the dagger strike on Sersi is not described on the cited page.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Peter Quill; Guardians of the Galaxy films, Avengers: Infinity War, Avengers: Endgame)
characters.summary: Star-Lord is a Ravager-raised pilot and marksman who fights with Kree-made quad blasters, flies on jet boot attachments and wears a collapsible helmet. He briefly gained Celestial powers fighting Ego but lost them on Ego's death.

techniques: Quad blasters (non-lethal stun and lethal plasma modes)
Celestial energy powers (temporary, vs Ego only)

weaknesses: Prone to emotional outbursts (his rage at Thanos broke Mantis's hold on Titan)
mobility: Jet boot attachments flight, including zero-gravity maneuvering
limitations: Lost his Celestial powers upon Ego's death

sources.supports: Ronan defeat (dance-off distraction, team uses Power Stone), Ego fight with Celestial powers and their loss, Titan fight vs Thanos.
Quad blasters, jet boots, collapsible helmet, skilled pilot, holding the Power Stone with his friends, loss of Celestial powers, rage attack on Thanos.
Jet Boot Attachments used for flight in Guardians of the Galaxy, Infinity War and Endgame.

feats.claim: Held the Power Stone together with his new friends at the end of Guardians of the Galaxy.
Kept Ego occupied in combat with his newfound Celestial powers until Baby Groot planted a bomb on Ego's brain.
Flew through deep space on Knowhere with his jet boots to reach Gamora.

notableResults.note: Team win: Quill distracted Ronan with a dance-off while the others freed the Power Stone, which the group used to disintegrate Ronan.
Team win: Quill held Ego off with Celestial powers while Groot planted the bomb that killed him.
Team fight on Titan; the group had Thanos subdued by Mantis until Quill's enraged attack broke her hold, contributing to the Snap.

campaignTags.claim: Jet Boot Attachments propel him through the air
Kree-made quad blasters with stun/plasma modes and a collapsible helmet
Raised as a Ravager, he is a highly skilled pilot

unknowns: Gravity mines and electric batons were not supported by the opened pages; removed.
Original cited MCU wiki Star-Lord page could not be opened; replaced with the sources listed.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Netflix Marvel series: Daredevil and The Defenders; Scott Glenn)
characters.summary: Stick is a blind sensei and master martial artist of the Chaste who trained Matt Murdock and raised and trained Elektra. He fought the Hand across Daredevil and The Defenders until Elektra killed him.
weaknesses: Human physical vulnerability to lethal trauma (stabbed to death by Elektra)
limitations: Cut off his own right hand to escape captivity in The Defenders

sources.supports: Netflix Stick (Scott Glenn): training Matt and Elektra, Chaste, fights with Matt, Sowande and Elektra, self-amputation, death.

feats.claim: Trained Matt Murdock and raised and trained Elektra.
Rescued Matt and Elektra from the Hand.
Cut off his own right hand to free himself from his restraints.

notableResults.note: After Stick killed the Black Sky, Matt defeated him and Stick agreed to leave the city.
Decapitated Sowande when he tried to kidnap Danny Rand.
Elektra disarmed him in a sword fight and stabbed him to death.

unknowns: Heightened senses / radar sense, staff fighting and pressure-point targeting are not clearly attributed to the Netflix version on the opened page; removed pending a source.
Whether he led the Chaste; the opened page only calls them his fellow associates.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, 2017; Chris Sullivan)
characters.summary: Taserface is a Ravager in Yondu's crew who led a mutiny when he judged Yondu to be going soft, killing Yondu's loyalists and imprisoning Yondu and Rocket. Yondu escaped and killed him and the mutineers, but Taserface first alerted the Sovereign.

techniques: Leading a Ravager crew in mutiny

weaknesses: Overconfident; underestimated Yondu and was killed by him after the escape
limitations: Ordinary Ravager with no special powers shown

sources.supports: Mutiny against Yondu, killing loyalists, contacting the Sovereign, death in the ship explosion.
Taserface's mutiny, imprisoning Rocket and Yondu aboard the Eclector, alerting the Sovereign, and Yondu killing him.

feats.claim: Led a mutiny against Yondu Udonta and killed those still loyal to him.
Imprisoned Rocket and Yondu aboard the Eclector.

notableResults.note: After Kraglin freed Yondu, Rocket and Groot, Yondu killed Taserface and the mutineers; Taserface alerted the Sovereign before dying.

unknowns: Energy rifles, armor plating and starship piloting were not supported by the opened pages; removed (pilot tag dropped).
Original cited MCU wiki Taserface page could not be opened.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Antonia Dreykov; Black Widow, 2021; Thunderbolts*, 2025)
characters.summary: Taskmaster is Antonia Dreykov, rebuilt by her father's Red Room after the Budapest bombing. Her implant and helmet let her mimic the fighting style of anyone she sees, and she uses a shield, sword and bow. Natasha Romanoff freed her from the Red Room's chemical control, and she was later shot dead by Ghost in Thunderbolts*.

mechanisms: Collapsible shield deployed from her vambrace

weaknesses: Must see a style to copy it
Can be neutralized by the antidote to the Red Room's chemical control (as Natasha did)
limitations: Mimicry depends on her suit/helmet systems
Under Dreykov's chemical mind control (no free will) until freed

sources.supports: Antonia's background, implant, mimicry helmet, shield, sword, bow, claws, styles of Captain America, Black Panther and Hawkeye, freedom from chemical control.
Taskmaster's attacks on Romanoff, Budapest pursuit, Red Room fights, freefall battle and antidote; mimicry of anyone she sees.
Taskmaster shot dead by Ava Starr (Ghost) early in Thunderbolts*.

feats.claim: Mimicked Captain America's and Black Panther's fighting styles and Hawkeye's archery.
Mimicked the actions of anyone she saw after Dreykov's implant saved her life.

notableResults.note: Romanoff escaped her first attack and evaded her in Budapest; in the final freefall battle Romanoff subdued her and used an antidote vial to free her.
Shot dead by Ava Starr early in the film.

campaignTags.claim: Mimicry helmet, vambrace-deployed collapsible shield, explosive arrows and retractable claws

unknowns: Original feat listed Black Widow's style among those copied; the opened pages name Captain America, Black Panther and Hawkeye.
Full circumstances of her death scene in Thunderbolts* (the opened page says only that Ava Starr shot her).
Original cited MCU wiki Taskmaster page could not be opened.
cyborg tag not applied (reviewer): Dreykov's implant/chip is documented, but the sources do not establish a cybernetic body; revisit if a source describes her as a cyborg.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Avengers: Infinity War, 2018; Avengers: Endgame, 2019)
characters.summary: Thanos is a Titan warlord of immense strength and durability who wears golden battle armor and fights with a massive two-bladed sword. Without any Infinity Stone he beat the Hulk in hand-to-hand combat.

mechanisms: Titan durability (withstood the Hulk's full-force assault and Iron Man's energy blasts)
Two-bladed sword strong enough to deflect Stormbreaker and Mjolnir

weaknesses: Can be restrained by a coordinated team (subdued by Mantis on Titan until the hold broke)
Not invulnerable: survived but was grievously wounded by Stormbreaker
limitations: No energy projection of his own; his cosmic powers come from the Infinity Stones

sources.supports: Hulk defeated without Infinity Stones, two-bladed sword, golden armor, durability vs Hulk and Iron Man, Sanctuary II, Endgame fates.
Hulk fight without the Power Stone; Titan fight where Thanos stabbed Stark with his own sword.

feats.claim: Defeated the Hulk in hand-to-hand combat without aid from the Power Stone, rendering him unconscious.
His two-bladed sword deflected strikes from Stormbreaker and Mjolnir.

notableResults.note: Beat Hulk unconscious aboard the Statesman without using the Power Stone.
On Titan he tore the sword from Stark's hand and stabbed him in the abdomen with it, ending the fight.

unknowns: The Titan win over Iron Man came while Thanos was collecting the Infinity Stones; how much the partially filled gauntlet contributed is not detailed on the opened pages.
Exact biological limits of Titan longevity and resistance to energy attacks.
Original cited MCU wiki Thanos page could not be opened; replaced with the sources listed.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics, Marvel: The End (2003); comics form, not MCU
characters.summary: In Marvel: The End, Thanos destroyed the Celestial Order's machinery and absorbed the Heart of the Universe's power, becoming more powerful than he was with the Infinity Gauntlet and one with everyone and everything, with even the Living Tribunal reduced to a part of him. He finally restored the universe and erased himself.

techniques: Universal-scale power (absorbed cosmic beings and the universe into himself)
Time travel (went back to destroy the Celestial Order)

mechanisms: Cosmic beings sent to stop him failed

weaknesses: Could be persuaded to sacrifice himself (Adam Warlock talked him into it)
limitations: Could not correct the universe's fatal flaw even with the Heart's power; the only fix was to destroy and rebuild the universe
characters.formDifferences: Unlike base Thanos, he absorbed the Heart of the Universe and became more powerful than with the Infinity Gauntlet, one with all existence (comics only).

sources.supports: Thanos absorbing the Heart of the Universe, its scale, time travel, killing Akhenaten, absorbing the universe, its limitation and his self-erasure.

feats.claim: Absorbed the Heart of the Universe and became one with everyone and everything; even the Living Tribunal became a part of him.
Travelled back in time and destroyed the Celestial Order before they found the Heart.
Absorbed the cosmic beings and the entire universe into himself.

notableResults.note: Killed Akhenaten when he tried to stop Doom from killing Thanos's past self.

unknowns: Comics-only form filed under the MCU pool; it has no MCU appearance.
Original record cited only the MCU wiki base Thanos page and claimed absolute omnipotence and invulnerability; replaced with the comics source, which describes a hard limit (the uncorrectable flaw).

characters.summary: Thanos wielding the completed Infinity Gauntlet in the Battle of Wakanda: he phased Banner out of space with the Space Stone, blasted Captain America with a Power Stone shockwave, reversed Vision's destruction with the Time Stone, and completed the Snap despite Thor's Stormbreaker strike.

techniques: The Snap (erased half of all life)

mechanisms: Time Stone reversal (undid Vision's destruction to take the Mind Stone)
Base Titan durability (survived Stormbreaker buried in his chest)

weaknesses: His body can still be gravely wounded (Thor buried Stormbreaker in his chest)
limitations: The Snap scorched and burned the Gauntlet and his left arm
characters.formDifferences: Adds the completed Infinity Gauntlet with all six stones to base Thanos, giving him the Snap, Power Stone shockwaves, Space Stone teleportation and Time Stone reversal.

sources.supports: The Snap, Stormbreaker strike to Thanos's chest, and the Gauntlet and left arm scorched by the Snap.
Thanos's use of the Space, Power and Time Stones against the defenders in Wakanda, the Snap, and his teleporting away.

feats.claim: Used the Time Stone to reverse Vision's destruction.
Activated the Gauntlet and wiped out half of all life in the universe.

notableResults.opponent: Avengers and Wakandan defenders (Battle of Wakanda)
notableResults.note: Brushed aside Banner, Captain America, Black Panther and others with the stones, survived Thor's Stormbreaker strike, completed the Snap and teleported away.

campaignTags.claim: Teleported away with the Space Stone after the Snap

unknowns: 'Gamma radiation' damage and 'vulnerable during the gesture' claims were not supported by the opened pages; removed. The Snap's documented cost is a scorched gauntlet and burned left arm.
Original cited MCU wiki Infinity Gauntlet page could not be opened; replaced with the sources listed.
Whether a non-Titan could survive wearing the complete gauntlet.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics, 'Thanos Wins' (Thanos vol. 2, Donny Cates and Geoff Shaw); comics form, not MCU
characters.summary: King Thanos is a far-future Thanos who wiped out all sentient life and rules a wasteland from a compound built on a fallen Celestial's bones. His Black Right Hand is Frank Castle's Cosmic Ghost Rider, and he kept the Hulk chained as a pet. With his younger self's help he killed the Silver Surfer (the Fallen One) with Surtur's Sword of Doom.
weaknesses: Aged: his younger self systematically took him apart
limitations: Needed his younger self's help to defeat the Fallen One
characters.formDifferences: A far-future Thanos who has already won, ruling a dead universe with Cosmic Ghost Rider as his enforcer and wielding Surtur's Sword of Doom; older and weaker in single combat than his present-day self (comics only).

sources.supports: King Thanos's wasteland rule, Celestial-bone compound, chained Hulk, Cosmic Ghost Rider, Surtur's Sword of Doom killing the Silver Surfer and Hulk, needing present Thanos vs the Fallen One.
King Thanos wiped out all sentient life; present-day Thanos beating him in their fight; aftermath with Lady Death.

feats.claim: Wiped out all sentient life in his future.

notableResults.note: With present-day Thanos's help; King Thanos drove Surtur's Sword of Doom through the Surfer's chest.
The younger Thanos systematically took him apart and walked away after he begged.

unknowns: Comics-only form filed under the MCU pool; it has no MCU appearance.
His personal powers beyond the sword are not detailed on the opened pages.
His fate after the story (CBR implies he vanished; a later Guardians issue reportedly shows him as Death).
